difficulty_reason: The proof identifies the connected components of ranked comparisons through maximal monochromatic runs and counts rankings whose factorial component sizes are simultaneously small. New stars-and-bars tail bounds and an explicit Stirling analysis recover the larger-side binary-search term missing from a sensitivity-only lower bound. The complete source-local cross-inversion anti-concentration construction then excludes the middle values where coarsening to the Mann–Whitney objective could merge components; general tree bounds and local analytic lemmas are supporting context, not extra units.
